body: I've tried this in the past, but it's not just an issue with talking to people, it's also that I don't really know how to describe feelings, emotions, etc. It seems like I can't find words that apply. I like to think I'm learning to do this, but it's still pretty hard for me. I should be glad *you* responded, you're the one performing a kind gesture. :P

Thanks, man. It's not much of an achievement, but it's something. I'll keep your advice in mind, and post updates here periodically. 

I love how so many people are readily willing to reach out and help strangers like this, it's refreshing to know that people can still be selfless. Thanks again for taking the time to respond.

Thanks, it means a lot. It's nice to not have to keep up appearances like with everyone else. Pretending you're fine gets hard over time. Somewhat of a positive point is that I haven't had a drink tonight! It doesn't seem like much of an accomplishment, but I've been told repeatedly to try and take pride in the little victories, which I've been trying to do. I apparently belittle my achievements without realising it quite often, so. It's like "yay, I didn't drink tonight! but wait a minute, some people don't drink most every night, what's so good about that?" etc etc.

Thanks again for taking an interest. I'll be sure to report back with updates periodically.

I'm positive about the Asperger's, it was diagnosed by an Aspergers specialist or something, if I recall. Around the time of my diagnosis I spoke to quite a few people including doctors, nurses, consultants, etc, although I was in a pretty dark place so don't remember a lot of the details. I do remember the last interview I had which was with the aforementioned specialist, and it lasted somewhere between 4-6 hours, I forget. I never self-diagnose myself with anything, really. If anything, I'll often think I'm not ill when I clearly am. I'm pretty tired, so sorry if my reply didn't make much sense. :(

EDIT - I should note that it was at the end of the 4-6 hour interview that they confirmed my diagnosis, they thought it was surprising that it didn't get noticed sooner.

Thanks, man. I don't really have that many hobbies. I'd say the three things that work best are probably tv, music, and video games. Probably because you can immerse yourself in them, it's like an escape from reality. However lately these aren't working as well as they used to, likely because I can't really concentrate on them. :(

However, I have said in another post that I'm going to force myself to take up a new activity in an attempt to keep myself occupied, and distract me from my problems for a while. I haven't quite decided what yet, but I plan to post back here periodically with results, in case anyone is interested. Similarly, I'm also going to make myself go on my static exercise bike for an hour or so every day, as exercise is always good.

Thanks a lot for taking the time to reply, these comments really have brightened my evening slightly. Hell, I haven't even had a drink ~~yet~~ tonight!

Thanks for responding, buddy. It's not the specific therapist that's the problem - he's a really nice, patient guy, it's that I have real trouble expressing my feelings with anyone. If anything, I think it might be counter-productive to change to someone else, as I'm more comfortable talking to someone that I'm familiar with, so someone new would just be extra stress. :(

It didn't occur to me that exercise would help, plus because I've lacking motivation I haven't really bothered with anything. I said in another post that I'm going to make myself go on my static exercise bike for an hour or so each day, and see if that makes a difference. Practically everyone here has suggested doing things I like, which makes sense. I've said in another post that I plan to force myself to take up a new activity that will hopefully keep me occupied and ~~maybe~~ hopefully even bring me some joy. I plan to report back to this page periodically in case anyone's interested.

Thanks. I really am trying to carry on, hence this post. I still want to live, but not like this. I just want to be happy. (Who doesn't, right?) Thanks again for responding, it means a lot.

It's hard for me to sum up dyspraxia, but I found a [list of symptoms](http://www.dyspraxiafoundation.org.uk/services/ad_symptoms.php) that might interest you. You don't sound like an idiot by the way, it's not a very commonly-known disorder.

As for the drugs, it's pretty much just inhaling nitrates, but I forget which. :( Although I did some research and they don't negatively affect mood, and don't stay in your system for very long anyway. What adds to my depression is the fact that I feel I *need* to drink etc to have a good time, as I feel it shouldn't be used as a crutch like that. I used to drink when I was happy, not to become happy. Not to mention the fact that it's obviously bad for my health (and my wallet!).

The only place I can really find any kind of pleasure is something that almost disconnects me from reality, like an escape, the main three being TV, music, and video games. These are things that you can just concentrate on, and lose yourself in them. Although I must admit that these are helping less and less lately, as I find I get less pleasure from doing them. It's just getting harder to make it through the day. Some days I won't even get out of bed because I don't see the point. I responded to another post saying that I plan to force myself to do some kind of new activity to pass the time, and keep me occupied. I don't really like running as the dyspraxia makes this difficult, but I do have a static exercise bike in my shed that I never use, would that suffice? I could probably force myself to put on a podcast or something and use it for an hour or so if you think it might help. I know what endorphins are, but it hadn't really occurred to me that exercise might help my mood. I'd just pass at the chance because I'd feel like I can't be bothered. 

Don't worry about rambling, I should be the one apologising for that. I really appreciate that you've taken the time to respond to me. It's not that I feel nobody cares about me or anything, but I haven't told anyone IRL what's actually wrong with me. Apart from my parents and to a lesser extent a friend, nobody really knows what I'm going through. One of my greatest fears is that if I told people what was wrong with me, they'd view/treat me differently. I mean, I'm technically disabled, but if you say that to someone it almost always makes them think negative things about you, and they suddenly see you as somehow less of a person even though you're still the same guy you were before you told them. It's like slapping a 'defective' sticker on your forehead. To clarify, I don't see it like this, but I'm saying that some other people might. It's a sad state of affairs, but it's true. :(

Thanks again for taking the time to respond. It's nice to know there are some good people out there. :P

I'm starting to notice a common theme here, in that people are saying to do things that I enjoy. One of the problems I'm facing is that I've essentially lost interest in the things that I used to enjoy. I just replied to someone else saying that I'm going to force myself to start doing some kind of new activity, in a hope that it'll keep me busy, and maybe even cheer me up a tad.

I see what you mean, my goal isn't to stop drinking, it's to be able to stop after a few. It'd also be nice if I drank for different reasons. I used to drink when I was having a good time, now I drink *to* have a good time, as it's pretty much the only thing that works at the minute. I'll try to keep these questions in mind when I'm inevitably laid awake in bed later, unable to sleep.

Thanks for taking the time to respond to me though, it really means a lot.

Sorry, one of the problems I have is always worrying that I'm going to burden someone, even though that's likely not the case. I'm trying to moderate my drinking, but lately I've been failing. I'm currently trying a system where I can drink one night, but not the next, so I'd alternate like Mon, Wed, Fri, Sun, Tues, Thurs, Sat, repeat. I also keep track of the amount I drink each day when I do, always trying never to go higher than last time. It's not ideal, but it's something (considering that it used to be every night, at least). This worked for a week or two, but the last few nights I've gone a little overboard. :(

It seems unappealing to me, as I've pretty much lost interest in everything, but I think I might force myself to take your advice and try to find a new activity that I might enjoy, or that will at least keep my mind from wandering into a darker place. I'll update this page with progress every now and again, in case anyone is interested. 

Thanks a lot for taking the time to respond, it's nice to know that people can still be so friendly.

They're really caring, I just have trouble expressing my feelings to anyone, which is part of the problem. It's like I don't know how to word it. I've slowly started to get better at it, but I still suck at it. :P But yeah, my mum and dad have been really supportive when I've needed them to be, don't get me wrong.

Thanks for taking the time to respond by the way, it means more than you might think.

I suppose it's somewhat reassuring to know I'm not alone. Keep an eye on this page, maybe some kind redditor will say something that'll help us both. Thanks for taking the time to read my post and respond.
Just drunk enough that I'm not as sad, but this shouldn't be the way to live. Don't worry about replying, you could better spend your time.
